_comment: A21 Rear Panel PCA -- test point expectations.
Fifteen wire-loop test points, all fifteen in the parts list (TP1-15,
stock 816090) and all fifteen on the locator drawing. Their nets are named
only in the sheet 1 legend of 5700A-1009, which also gives the sheet zone
each is drawn in. A21 generates no supply of its own: +5 LOGIC and +/-12 V
come from the Digital Power Supply (A19, Table 2-2) and +5 LH, -5 LH and
+5 RLH from the Regulator/Guard Crossing assembly (A17, Table 2-10), so
each rail's nominal and band are those tables' values, and a rail that is
out of band here is checked at its source before anything on this board
is suspected. The serial lines and PA COM have no published value.
The board is split into an unguarded half referenced to +5 LOGIC COMMON
(TP4) and a guarded half referenced to LH COM (TP14) and RLH COM (TP15);
PA COM (TP10) is the analog common of the boost interface. Never tie a

12V.label: +/-12 V unguarded supplies (from A19), RS-232-C drivers

LH.label: +5 LH / -5 LH guarded logic supplies (from A17)

PACOM.label: PA COM, the boost interface analog common

testpoints.source: Sheet 1 legend (PG1B8); value from Table 2-2 (A19 TP12, +5V)
testpoints.note: The +5 LOGIC rail as it arrives from A19 on J9. Table 2-2 gives 5.2 V +/-5 % at A19's own TP12 (5.2 rather than 5.0 because of the germanium diode under the regulator's ground pin); the same band is used here because nothing on the way is meant to drop it. Low here but right at A19 TP12 means J9, the motherboard cable or a short on this board.

testpoints.source: Sheet 1 legend (PG1B8); value from Table 2-2 (A19 TP8)
testpoints.note: From A19 on J9. Feeds the 1488 RS-232-C line driver U6 (pin 14) and the U18 clock amplifier. Table 2-2's band for the rail at its source.

testpoints.source: Sheet 1 legend (PG1B7); value from Table 2-2 (A19 TP10, sign corrected there)
testpoints.note: From A19 on J9. Feeds the 1488 driver U6 (pin 1) only, so a dead -12 V shows as an RS-232-C transmit line stuck at one level while everything else on the board works.

Return for the unguarded half of the board: +5 LOGIC, +/-12 V, the IEEE-488 and RS-232-C interfaces and the DUART. The meter's low lead for TP1-TP3 and TP5-TP9. Chassis, via the connector shells, is a separate net.

testpoints.condition: Power on, remote traffic on the RS-232-C port
testpoints.note: DUART U5 channel A transmit (pin 30, active low), before the 1488 driver U6D turns it into the TX line on J2 pin 2. TTL levels; idles high. No level is published -- look for activity when the instrument answers on the serial port.

testpoints.condition: Power on, remote traffic on the RS-232-C port
testpoints.note: DUART U5 channel A receive (pin 31), after the 1489 receiver U7C has converted the RX line from J2 pin 3 to TTL. Idles high. Activity here with no response from the instrument points at U5 or the CPU interface rather than at the port.

DUART U5's serial clock output (pin 28), derived from RPCLK, which PLD U8 buffers from the 3.6864 MHz clock that U18 regenerates from the CPU's 200 mV differential clock. No clock here means no serial ports and no 5725A control: check U18 (zone A6 on sheet 1) and RP3.68MHZ first.

DUART U5 channel B receive (pin 10): the 5725A's reply, B-SCR from J7 pin 17 through receiver U7B. Also brought out on J10 pins 2/3 for software test. Idles high; silent with a 5725A connected means the cable interlock B-CINT* or the amplifier itself.
DUART U5 channel B transmit (pin 11), the command stream to the 5725A, before driver U6B puts it on B-SCT at J7 pin 18. Idles high.

The Power Amplifier common as it passes through the boost interface: J8 to K7 to J7 (BPA COM). Analog, guarded, and a different net from LH COM. Use it as the low lead only for the boost-signal lines on sheet 4.

testpoints.source: Sheet 1 legend (PG5D6); value from Table 2-10 (A17 TP11)
testpoints.note: The guarded logic supply from A17 arriving on J8, feeding the 82C55 (U14), the LF356 (U13, pin 7) and the relay drivers' logic. Table 2-10's band at its source.

testpoints.source: Sheet 1 legend (PG5D6); value from Table 2-10 (A17 TP15)
testpoints.note: From A17 on J8. On this board it supplies only U13's negative rail (pin 4), so a missing -5 LH shows as the 5205A sense amplifier stuck at a rail while all the digital control still works.

testpoints.source: Sheet 1 legend (PG5D5); value from Table 2-10 (A17 TP14, +5.55 V to +6.40 V)
testpoints.note: The relay supply from A17 on J8: the coil rail for all twelve relays and the +VS of the two 5801 drivers U16 and U17, through choke L1. Sits deliberately above +5 LH. Sagging here under relay load points at A17's regulator or J8, not at this board.
Guarded logic return from A17 via J8: the low lead for TP11 and TP12 and for anything in the 82C55 / relay-driver circuit on sheet 5.
Relay supply return from A17 via J8: the low lead for TP13. Kept separate from LH COM so relay coil current does not flow through the logic return.

probePoints.label: U18 pin 4 -- RP3.68MHZ
probePoints.note: The regenerated 3.6864 MHz TTL clock, made by NE522 differential comparator U18 from the CPU's 200 mV p-p 3.6864MHZCLK / 3.6864MHZCLK* pair on J9. Everything serial on the board -- both DUART channels and the TMS9914 -- runs from this. A flat line here with the CPU clock present on J9 means U18, R8, R10 or the +/-12 V it needs.

probePoints.label: J8 pin 34 -- RLH COM from the motherboard
probePoints.source: Sheet 5 (zone C8); a return, so the expectation is that it is one
probePoints.note: Where the guarded returns enter the board. More than a few tens of millivolts between here and TP15 means a bad J8 contact carrying relay current.
